title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.25430v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. tldr: 该论文将模型合并的可组合性形式化为任务向量集合的性质，证明合并模型的超额损失由跨任务曲率重叠与更新带符号对齐构成的干涉泛函控制，并提出一种曲率引导的正则化微调方法，使合并模型在满足可组合性判据的同时保持标准的非凸收敛速率。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes composability of merged fine-tuned models as a property of task vector collections, proves the merged model's excess loss is governed by an interference functional of cross-task curvature overlap and signed update alignment, and introduces a curvature-guided regularizer that guarantees composability at the standard non-convex convergence rate.
